CVE-2026-107243.description:
The Node.js web service on VOS (previously Versa FlexVNF) is used for URL-based Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) of the VOS appliance and is not required after provisioning is complete. The express-session middleware in server.js is configured with a hardcoded secret that is identical across all VOS appliances and is used to sign session cookies. An attacker who obtains a valid session ID from any source can compute the correct HMAC-SHA256 signature and forge a session cookie that the server accepts as legitimate. Because the secret is shared across all VOS appliances, a forged cookie is accepted by any VOS appliance in the deployment.

Versa’s security hardening guide for Hubs, Branches, and Controllers recommends disabling the Node.js web service after the initial provisioning of the VOS device. This vulnerability is not exploitable on VOS devices where the Node.js web service has been disabled.

CVE-2026-121139.title: Rapid7 Metasploit Framework Web Service unauthenticated bootstrap window allows creation of an administrator account without authentication
CVE-2026-121139.description:
The Rapid7 Metasploit msf-ws suffers from a missing authentication vulnerability whereby the REST API grants an unauthenticated "bootstrap" exemption so that the very first administrator can be created when the users table is empty. While the table is empty, POST /api/v1/users is exempt from authentication by design: the route handler calls warden.authenticate!(scope: :admin_api), which resolves to AdminApiToken. The inherited ApiToken#authenticate! short-circuits and returns success!() whenever msf.auth_initialized is false, without ever evaluating AdminApiToken's administrator check. In that state the endpoint creates a user — including an administrator — for an entirely unauthenticated caller.

This issue has been fixed in version 6.5.9.

CVE-2026-121632.title: Data::MuForm versions through 0.05 for Perl render attribute values and option labels into HTML without escaping
CVE-2026-121632.description:
Data::MuForm versions through 0.05 for Perl render attribute values and option labels into HTML without escaping.

process_attrs writes each attribute value into the markup as is. The select, radio group and checkbox group renderers pass each option to it, so an option's value becomes an unescaped attribute. Option and option group labels are also unescaped, the group label inside a label attribute and the others in element content.

Any application whose option list is built from data rather than literals, using an options_<field_name> method, a build_options method or a DBIC model, allows attacker-influenced text in an option value or label that can embed JavaScript in rendered pages. Attribute values built from data, such as through element_attr, are affected the same way.

CVE-2026-133626.title: FlowIntel: Resource Exhaustion via Sparse CSV/JSON Table Expansion During File-to-Note Conversion
CVE-2026-133626.description:
FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU.

The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel
- Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note

Impact:
- Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users
- No confidentiality or integrity impact

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

CVE-2026-62320.title: Netatalk: afpd unauthenticated DSI request smuggling via silent dsi_len truncation in dsi_tcp_open()
CVE-2026-62320.description: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 1.5.0 until 4.5.1, dsi_tcp_open in libatalk/dsi/dsi_tcp.c silently limits the bytes read from an unauthenticated DSI frame received on TCP/548 to server_quantum when the attacker-controlled dsi_len is larger, without rejecting the frame or draining the declared remainder. The same silent dsi_len truncation pattern exists in libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c. The leftover bytes remain queued on the TCP connection and the next dsi_stream_receive call interprets them as a new DSI header and payload, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to smuggle one or more additional attacker-controlled DSI frames into the same connection. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.

CVE-2026-99591.title: iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size
CVE-2026-99591.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size

IOMMU can perform out-of-bounds read of the device table entry (DTE)
that is adjacent to the last DTE and falls outside the device table.
For example, if the device table can hold 0 to N-1 entries, then the
IOMMU can be made to fetch the Nth entry, which falls outside the
device table.

The device table is owned by the hypervisor (HV) and is assigned in 4KB
pages that are contiguous in system physical address (SPA). If the
out-of-bound DTE falls on a guest-owned page, then the guest can exploit
this bug to setup malicious table walks to corrupt HV pages and/or bring
down the system. Note that this bug does not manifest when the device
table size is set to its maximum size of 2MB.

Therefore, force the device table size to the maximum 2MB on affected
processors. These are CPU family 0x17 (Zen1/Zen2) through family 0x1a
(Zen5/BRH).
